newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian oil firm sees 1997 pre-tax at HRK 253 mln.
newsitem.headline: Croatian oil firm sees 1997 pre-tax at HRK 253 mln.

text.p: Croatian oil firm INA Industrija Nafte sees its group 1997 pre-tax profit at 253 million kuna ($46 million) after a financial recovery expected this year.
In 1995, the state-owned monopolist posted a net loss of 1.2 billion kuna, accumulated mostly in its core business of oil and natural gas exploration, production and supply.
According to its 1997 business plan, published in the weekly corporate newsletter, INA will seek to boost its output of all oil derivatives by 12 percent to 4.8 million tonnes.
Exports would account for 37 percent of gross sales, with the rest sold on the domestic market, but three was no figure for the expected total income.
Still, INA said it would reinvest 1.15 billion kuna next year into long-term assets, probably production facilities.
It plans to refine 5.25 million tonnes of crude, of which some 19 percent would be extracted from Croatian oilfields and the rest would have to be imported.
Its own production of crude and condensates would rise by three percent from this year's estimate to 1.75 million tonnes.

Natural gas output is pencilled in at 1.8 billion cubic metres and the company plans to import another 1.0 billion cu m to meet the country's consumption needs. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
